archetype.name: Game Manager (backup)
archetype.definition: A low-risk, short-area distributor who keeps an offense on schedule with quick completions underneath but has not yet shown he can drive the ball between the numbers or finish drives.

report.headline: A capable short-game backup whose intermediate throws keep turning into turnovers
report.take:
Bagent is Chicago's QB2 behind Caleb Williams, who has started every week since Week 6. His 2026 is three appearances: a 14%-snap cameo against Minnesota, a full game in the 23-12 win over the Jets, and his one start, a 31-7 loss at Green Bay. Treat the season line as a backup's sample, not a verdict. It still shows a consistent shape, one that matches his 2023 tape: accurate and efficient within ten yards, shaky beyond it.

The split tells the story. On throws of 0-9 air yards he is completing 72.4% with +0.23 EPA per attempt and a 62% success rate, which is starter-quality work. On 10-19 yard throws he is at 41.2% with a CPOE of -13.8 and all three of his interceptions, worth -0.446 EPA per attempt. That gap explains both games. Against the Jets he barely got pressured (5.6%), threw short (5.8 intended air yards) and posted +7.9 EPA. At Green Bay his aggressiveness jumped to 33.3%, his bad-throw rate hit 23.8%, and two picks sank him to -10.3 EPA. He has also taken a far more aggressive approach than in 2023, when only 12.6% of his throws went into tight windows against 25.45% now. The added risk has bought turnovers, not explosive plays.

The numbers flatter him in one place and probably undersell him in another. The 1.7 CPOE and 65.6% completion rate ride on dump-offs and screens; his adjusted net yards per dropback of 4.53 ranks 43rd of 47, and he has no touchdown passes. The 40% pressure-to-sack rate looks alarming, but it comes from a handful of pressured dropbacks, and in 2023 he ranked 4th in that stat. The red-zone line (-0.339 EPA, 46.7% completions) and the zero-TD rate are partly a small sample, but they fit a passer who can't yet threaten the intermediate window when the field shrinks.

The outlook is simple. Barring a Williams injury he holds a clipboard, and Case Keenum being inactive as the emergency third QB confirms Bagent as the sole active backup. If he is pressed into duty, Chicago's offense (9th in pass EPA, with Rome Odunze at +0.587 EPA per target) gives him a sound supporting cast. He is a short-term caretaker for that offense, not a quarterback who elevates it.

strengths.title: Efficient, accurate underneath passing
strengths.body: His short throws are the best thing on his tape: 72.4% completions, a 5.6 CPOE and positive EPA on 0-9 yard attempts. It comes from quick processing and a willingness to take what's there, the same profile that produced an above-average success rate in 2023. That holds up across seasons, so it's the part of his game a coaching staff can lean on.

strengths.title: Keeps the pocket clean
strengths.body: He has been pressured on just 14.7% of dropbacks, 3rd-lowest among qualifiers, with a 2.84-second time to throw. Some of that is Chicago's line (8th in hit rate allowed). Much of it is his quick, underneath approach, which gets the ball out before pressure arrives. He also hasn't lost a fumble.

concerns.title: Intermediate window produces turnovers
concerns.body: All three interceptions came on 10-19 yard throws, where he completes 41.2% with a -13.8 CPOE. His tight-window rate has roughly doubled since 2023, so this looks less like bad luck than a passer trying throws he doesn't place well. That is a real flaw, and the main reason his one start collapsed.

concerns.title: No finishing power
concerns.body: Zero touchdowns on 64 attempts, and -0.339 EPA per play in the red zone. The TD rate will tick up with more volume, but an offense built on short completions stalls when the field compresses and the intermediate seams are the only openings.

concerns.title: The start went badly
concerns.body: In his lone start he posted -0.448 EPA per dropback with a -10.9 CPOE and two picks at Green Bay. One road game against a top-10 defense is thin evidence, but it showed how quickly things unravel when he can't play from ahead and has to push the ball.

trend.note: His three outings swing from a brief cameo to a +7.9 EPA game against the Jets to -10.3 EPA at Green Bay. He hasn't taken a meaningful snap since Williams returned in Week 6.

nextGame.headline: Likely inactive in practice; Tampa's defense would punish his weakness
nextGame.body:
Bagent goes into the Tampa Bay game as the backup, so the realistic expectation is that he doesn't play. If he does, Tampa is a hard draw. It ranks 2nd in pass EPA allowed and 2nd on short throws, which takes away the underneath game he lives on. It also allows few explosive passes, leaving him little room to make up for a stalled short game. The opening is that the Bucs rarely get home (28th in hit rate, 24th in sack rate), which suits a quick-release passer. Chicago as a 6-point home favorite also points toward a script where a backup would be asked to manage the game, not chase it.

On availability, Keenum being inactive as the emergency third QB makes Bagent the only active backup behind Williams; he is not in line to start. Kyle Monangai's absence trims the backfield but doesn't bear on Bagent. On Tampa's side, LB Yaya Diaby (MCL) is out, which weakens an already light pass rush. CB Josh Hayes remains on IR.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs. stingy underneath defense
keyMatchups.body: His best area, 0-9 yard throws, runs into a defense that ranks 2nd in EPA on short passes. If the underneath game is taken away, he would be pushed toward the intermediate throws where his interceptions have come.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Tampa pass rush
keyMatchups.body: Tampa ranks near the bottom in hitting and sacking quarterbacks, and Diaby is out. A clean pocket is where Bagent has been at his best, as in the Jets win.

nextGame.watch: Whether Caleb Williams finishes the game. Bagent's snaps only exist if he doesn't.

restOfSeason.body:
As long as Williams is healthy, Bagent's expected output is close to nothing, somewhere around 0-15 passing yards a game across the rest of the schedule. The more useful question is what a spot start would look like. Given his short-game efficiency, a good supporting cast and Chicago's run-leaning approach, a reasonable range is 150-220 passing yards with an interception about as likely as a touchdown.

His short accuracy and quick release should hold; they match his 2023 profile. The zero-TD rate should improve with volume. The 4.7% interception rate comes partly from small samples, but it will stay above average unless he dials back the tight-window throws. The 40% pressure-to-sack rate should regress toward his much better 2023 mark.

projections.stat: Passing yards / start (if pressed into duty)

swingFactors: Whether he dials back tight-window intermediate throws
Game script in any spot start

confidence.note: 64 attempts, one start, and a backup role that may yield no snaps.
